subject: Post-demo: Clarify cloud supplier roster & next steps for security review
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@medsys.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medsys.com, IT Procurement <procurement@medsys.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — SOC 2 / suppliers / DPA

Thanks for the demo today, Stephanie — appreciate the walkthrough. I wanted to capture our outstanding asks so we can get this into procurement quickly:

- SOC 2 status: do you have a SOC 2 Type II report or an attestation summary we can share with internal auditors?
- Subprocessor list: full roster of cloud suppliers and any downstream subprocessors that could handle customer data (storage, analytics, logging, monitoring).
- Data flow diagram: high-level path for PII and PHI when using your hosted API (where data persists, duration, and replication regions).
- Standard DPA: can you provide your standard DPA template?

If possible can you get these to us within the next 5 business days? Procurement wants to schedule a security call after they review.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
VP Product
Medsys Health
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@medsys.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, security@medsys.com, IT Procurement <procurement@medsys.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — SOC 2 / suppliers / DPA

Hi Elena — great meeting earlier, and really glad to hear Medsys is moving quickly on procurement. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

What we’ll provide by EOD Tue (21 Aug):
- SOC 2 summary (PDF) + process point of contact for auditor questions. We currently maintain SOC 2 Type II and can provide the summary and controls matrix; full reports are shared under NDA.
- Third-party roster (attached spreadsheet) listing primary cloud providers, managed logging, telemetry, and monitoring vendors; each row includes purpose, data types processed, and data residency.
- High-level data flow (inline and we’ll attach a diagram): shows token handling, KV cache behavior, and retention windows for hosted API.
- Our standard DPA (DOCX) for procurement to review.

Internal notes: Kimberly will attach the roster and the SOC summary; Ben will sync on contractual redlines if procurement suggests changes to the DPA.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll drop the attachments to this thread by EOD Tue.
2) Elena/procurement to confirm a 30-min security Q&A the week of Aug 28 if needed.
3) If you want the SOC 2 full report, we can execute an NDA and share the auditor package.

Let us know if any of that timeline is too aggressive.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Elena Martinez <elena@medsys.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, security@medsys.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — SOC 2 / suppliers / DPA

Hi all — attaching the initial artifacts we discussed. Attachment stubs are below; I can upload originals to the secure share if you want the full SOC package (we require a standard auditor NDA).

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_third_party_roster_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — columns: vendor_name, service_type, data_processed, region, subprocessors, contact, retention_policy
- SOC2-summary-2028-06.pdf (PDF) — 2-page executive summary and control highlights
- DPA-template-redwood-2028.docx (DOCX) — standard terms; track changes suggested by legal often land here

Quick notes on roster:
- Primary compute & storage: GCP (us-west1 primary, us-west2 DR) — customer data encrypted at rest; we use CMEK options for Dedicated/Private contracts.
- Logging & telemetry: Hosted telemetry retained 30 days by default; option to disable telemetry for Dedicated/Private.
- Monitoring/alerting: third party vendor NimbusOps — processes minimal metadata (no raw PII).
- Analytics/data-science: non-production copies are redacted; production pipelines do not persist prompt content beyond retention window unless customer opts into logging for fine-tune.

If you want, Ben can draft a short bullet list for procurement summarizing the most relevant items (data residency, encryption, access control) to expedite their review.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Program Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
From: Elena Martinez <elena@medsys.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medsys.com, security@medsys.com, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — SOC 2 / suppliers / DPA

Thanks Stephanie and Kim — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/security before we move to a call:

- Can you confirm whether any subprocessors are in EEA/APAC and, if so, which ones (we need region-specific controls for GDPR)?
- For NimbusOps (monitoring), please confirm whether they receive any prompt-level content or only operational telemetry.
- For the SOC 2 summary, is there a named contact for auditor questions and a typical NDA template we can use to speed the report exchange?

Procurement: can we tentatively schedule a 30-min call on Sept 1 or Sept 4 (ET) — please advise availability.

If you can answer the three bullets inline we’ll decide whether we need the Q&A call.

Elena
VP Product | Medsys Health
